metadata.question: In the Norwegian Sea during Septermber 1, 2019, is the water color at (50.282684, -58.944881) more milky than (50.415337, -54.128047)?

data.raw_code: The user is asking about water color in the Norwegian Sea at two specific points on September 1, 2019. They want to know if one location is "more milky" than the other. For water color analysis, I should use: 1. Sentinel-2 imagery which has good water color bands 2. Focus on bands that can detect turbidity/milkiness - typically using the blue/green/red bands and turbidity indices 3. A common approach is to use the Normalized Difference Turbidity Index (NDTI) = (Red - Green)/(Red + Green) 4. Higher NDTI values typically indicate more turbid/milky water Steps: 1. Define the two points as geometries 2. Get Sentinel-2 imagery for September 1, 2019 3. Check if collection has data 4. Calculate NDTI for both points 5. Compare the values to determine which is more milky I need to handle: - Cloud masking for Sentinel-2 - Valid pixel checks - Fallback strategies if no data ```javascript const ee = require('@google/earthengine'); const privateKey = require('../auth_keys/test-project-473922-29f05d49bed7'); async function runAnalysis() { // 1. Geometry & Time Definitions const point1 = ee.Geometry.Point([-58.944881, 50.282684]); const point2 = ee.Geometry.Point([-54.128047, 50.415337]); const date = '2019-09-01'; // 2. Data Acquisition - Sentinel-2 for water color analysis let s2Col = ee.ImageCollection('COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED') .filterDate(date, '2019-09-02') .filterBounds(ee.Geometry.Point([-58.944881, 50.282684])) .filterBounds(ee.Geometry.Point([-54.128047, 50.415337])); const colSize = s2Col.size().getInfo(); console.log(`Sentinel-2 Images: ${colSize}`); if (colSize === 0) { console.log("No Sentinel-2 data found."); console.log("C1"); return; } // Get least cloudy image const image = s2Col.sort('CLOUDY_PIXEL_PERCENTAGE').first(); // 3. Calculate Normalized Difference Turbidity Index (NDTI) // NDTI = (Red - Green)/(Red + Green) - higher values = more turbid/milky const ndti = image.normalizedDifference(['B4', 'B3']).rename('NDTI'); // 4. Extract values at both points const scale = 1000; const val1 = ndti.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.mean(), geometry: point1, scale: scale, maxPixels: 1e9 }).get('NDTI').getInfo(); const val2 = ndti.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.mean(), geometry: point2, scale: scale, maxPixels: 1e9 }).get('NDTI').getInfo(); // Check for valid pixels const count1 = image.select('B3').reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.count(), geometry: point1, scale: scale, maxPixels: 1e9 }).get('B3').getInfo(); const count2 = image.select('B3').reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.count(), geometry: point2, scale: scale, maxPixels: 1e9 }).get('B3').getInfo(); console.log(`Point1 NDTI: ${val1 !== null ? val1.toFixed(4) : 'null'}, Pixels: ${count1}`); console.log(`Point2 NDTI: ${val2 !== null ? val2.toFixed(4) : 'null'}, Pixels: ${count2}`); // 5. Validation & Final Answer if (val1 === null || val2 === null || count1 === 0 || count2 === 0) { console.log("C2"); } else if (isNaN(val1) || isNaN(val2) || val1 > 1 || val1 < -1 || val2 > 1 || val2 < -1) { console.log("C3"); } else if (val1 > val2) { console.log("Point1 is more milky (higher NDTI)"); console.log("A"); } else { console.log("Point2 is more milky or equal"); console.log("B"); } } async function initEE() { await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.data.authenticateViaPrivateKey(privateKey, resolve, reject); }); await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.initialize(null, null, resolve, reject); }); await runAnalysis(); } initEE(); ```
